title: Dead positions and insufficient material
summary: When no sequence of legal moves can lead to mate, the game is drawn at once.

steps.md:
A game is drawn immediately if **neither side can checkmate by any series of legal moves**: a **dead position**. Classic cases: K v K; K+B v K; K+N v K; K+B v K+B with bishops on the same colour; completely blocked pawn chains.

But **K+N+N v K is not dead**: mate cannot be forced, but it is possible if the defender blunders, so the game goes on.

steps.question: Is this a dead position?
choices: Yes: K+B v K can never mate
steps.explain: A single bishop (or knight) cannot mate even with help.

steps.question: Is this a dead position?
choices: No: mate with two knights is possible if Black errs
steps.explain: K+N+N v K cannot be forced, but a mating position exists, so the game is not dead.

steps.question: Both sides have one bishop, both on dark squares. Dead?
steps.explain: Same-coloured bishops can never cover the squares needed for mate. With opposite colours, a (silly) mate is possible, so that is not dead.

steps.question: Is this pawn wall position dead?
choices: Yes: nothing can ever move through
steps.explain: No pawn can move or capture, and neither king can cross: no mate is possible.

steps.prompt: Black's pawn is dangerous. Capture it to reach a dead position.
steps.explain: K+N v K: dead position, draw. Sometimes the best a defender can do is remove the last pawn.

steps.question: Your flag falls. You have a lone king; your opponent has king and knight. Result?
choices: Draw: the opponent cannot mate by any legal series of moves
steps.explain: Flag fall loses only if the opponent could still mate in some way (Art. 6.9).

steps.question: Retrieval check: is K+R v K a dead position?
steps.explain: Rook and king mate easily (box method).

steps.question: Retrieval check: which of these is NOT dead?
steps.explain: Two knights can mate if the defender helps.
